title: Glossopharyngeal (CN IX) transection: loss of general sensation at the tonsillar lining
vignette: A 66-year-old man is undergoing a procedure to control chronic throat pain due to Eagle syndrome, a condition frequently caused by a misshapen or elongated styloid process. During the procedure, the styloid process is trimmed surgically. However, the left glossopharyngeal nerve is accidentally transected. Which of the following is most likely to be seen as a result of this patient's nerve injury?

clues.text: left glossopharyngeal nerve is accidentally transected
clues.note: The glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) provides general sensation to the posterior pharynx/tonsils/middle ear, taste to the posterior third of the tongue, the afferent limb of the gag reflex, and parasympathetic secretion to the PAROTID gland.

whatMatters: The GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL nerve (CN IX) supplies general sensation to the tonsillar region, posterior pharynx, posterior third of the tongue, and middle ear (afferent gag reflex), taste to the posterior third of the tongue, and PAROTID secretion. Transection causes LOSS OF GENERAL SENSATION at the tonsillar lining. Answer D.
strategy: List CN IX functions and match: general sensation to tonsils/posterior pharynx/posterior tongue/middle ear, posterior-third taste, afferent gag reflex, parotid secretion, and one muscle (stylopharyngeus). Loss of tonsillar general sensation fits. Reject tongue deviation (hypoglossal CN XII), hoarseness (vagus/recurrent laryngeal CN X), anterior two-thirds taste (facial/chorda tympani CN VII), and submandibular gland secretion (facial CN VII via chorda tympani; CN IX serves the PAROTID).

options.text: Deviation of the protruded tongue toward the left
Hoarseness due to left vocal cord dysfunction
Impaired taste sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue
Loss of general sensation at the tonsillar lining
Reduced salivary secretion from the submandibular gland

eliminations.label: Tongue deviation - hypoglossal (CN XII)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: deviation of the protruded tongue (toward the lesion). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: tongue protrusion is controlled by the HYPOGLOSSAL nerve (CN XII), not CN IX. ✅ Correct if: hypoglossal nerve injury.

eliminations.label: Hoarseness - vagus/recurrent laryngeal (CN X)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: vocal cord dysfunction causing hoarseness. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: laryngeal muscles are innervated by the vagus/recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X), not CN IX. ✅ Correct if: recurrent laryngeal nerve injury.

eliminations.label: Anterior two-thirds taste - facial/chorda tympani (CN VII)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: taste from the front of the tongue. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: anterior two-thirds taste is carried by the chorda tympani (CN VII); CN IX carries POSTERIOR third taste. ✅ Correct if: facial nerve/chorda tympani injury.

eliminations.label: Submandibular gland secretion - facial (CN VII)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: reduced salivation from the submandibular gland. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: submandibular/sublingual secretion is via CN VII (chorda tympani -> submandibular ganglion); CN IX supplies the PAROTID gland (via the otic ganglion). ✅ Correct if: parotid secretion loss (CN IX) or facial nerve injury (submandibular).

reasoning: The glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) was transected
CN IX carries general sensation from the tonsillar region/posterior pharynx and the afferent gag reflex
So injury abolishes general sensation at the tonsillar lining (and the gag reflex afferent)
-> loss of general sensation at the tonsillar lining; answer D
mechanism: The GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL nerve (CN IX) exits the skull via the JUGULAR FORAMEN and has several functions: SOMATIC MOTOR to the stylopharyngeus (elevates the larynx in swallowing); PARASYMPATHETIC secretomotor to the PAROTID gland (inferior salivatory nucleus -> otic ganglion -> auriculotemporal nerve); GENERAL SENSORY to the posterior third of the tongue, the TONSILLAR region, upper pharynx (the AFFERENT limb of the GAG reflex), middle ear/eustachian tube, and the carotid body/sinus (chemo-/baroreceptors); and SPECIAL SENSORY (TASTE) to the posterior third of the tongue. Transection therefore causes LOSS OF GENERAL SENSATION over the tonsillar lining/posterior pharynx (with loss of the gag-reflex afferent) and loss of posterior-third taste, plus reduced parotid secretion. The distractors map to other nerves: tongue movement (CN XII), laryngeal phonation (CN X), anterior-tongue taste and submandibular/sublingual secretion (CN VII).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Anatomy > glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX): motor to stylopharyngeus; parasympathetic to PAROTID (otic ganglion); general sensation to posterior 1/3 tongue, tonsils, pharynx, middle ear (afferent gag); posterior 1/3 taste; carotid body/sinus.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: CN IX transection -> loss of general sensation at tonsils/posterior pharynx (afferent gag).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on glossopharyngeal nerve, afferent gag reflex, otic ganglion/parotid, or posterior-third taste? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Tongue deviation = CN XII; hoarseness = CN X; anterior taste/submandibular = CN VII; CN IX serves the PAROTID.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: CN IX = tonsil/posterior pharynx sensation + posterior 1/3 taste + parotid secretion + afferent gag; stylopharyngeus.

keywords.back: Posterior 1/3 tongue, tonsils, pharynx, middle ear (afferent gag)
Facial nerve (CN VII) via chorda tympani
Afferent CN IX; efferent CN X

firstAid.detail: Anatomy: tonsil/pharynx sensation, posterior taste, parotid, afferent gag.
Anatomy > CN XII (tongue), CN X (larynx), CN VII (anterior taste/submandibular).
Anatomy > afferent CN IX, efferent CN X.

memoryHook: CN IX is the throat's sensor - cut it and the tonsil/back-of-throat go numb (and the gag reflex loses its trigger); it feeds the PAROTID, not the submandibular gland.
